title: Mit Csináljak? – Asking What To Do

sections.title: The imperative, turned into a question
sections.content: To ask "what should I do?", Hungarian reuses the 1st-person imperative you met in the cooking unit, on the verb itself: Mit csináljak? ("What should I do?") and Mit tegyek? ("What should I do/put?", using the irregular imperative stem tegy- from tesz) are both standard ways to ask for guidance, not a command to anyone else.

items.english: My head hurts. What should I do?

items.spanish: Mit tegyek, ha nem alszom eleget?
items.english: What should I do if I don't sleep enough?

sections.content: You already used tegyél/tedd ("put!") as commands to someone else in the recipe unit — tegyek is the same imperative family, just in the "I" form, which naturally reads as "should I..." rather than a command.
